commands.fixtures: loopback HTTP fixture served by the probe; no production UI, dist bundle or user profile is loaded

method.hostWindow: hidden BrowserWindow, webviewTag=true, sandbox=true, contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false
method.guestPreferencesEnforced: will-attach-webview forces sandbox=true, contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false, webSecurity=true, preload removed
method.survivalProof: two executeJavaScript calls after the close attempt (incrementing counter + DOM node), plus isDestroyed() and getAllWebContents() membership
method.destroyedProof: destroyed event, isDestroyed()===true, absence from getAllWebContents(), and getWebContentsId() after teardown
method.boundedTimeouts: 50s per probe process, 60s per child, 2-3s per close/dialog wait

experiments.name: allow-none
experiments.purpose: Control: an unprotected page should be destroyed by a protected close.
experiments.expectation: close({waitForBeforeUnload:true}) destroys the guest and fires no will-prevent-unload.

experiments.name: refuse-onbeforeunload
experiments.purpose: Reproduce window.onbeforeunload=()=>false with the documented default (main never calls preventDefault).
experiments.expectation: The guest survives the protected close, stays scriptable, survives a second close, and closes after the handler is removed.

experiments.name: allow-via-preventDefault
experiments.purpose: Control for the documented escape hatch: preventDefault on will-prevent-unload permits unload.
experiments.expectation: preventDefault on will-prevent-unload makes the protected close destroy the guest.

experiments.name: refuse-addEventListener
experiments.purpose: Check whether modern addEventListener(beforeunload) + preventDefault/returnValue is honoured.
experiments.expectation: The guest survives the protected close and closes after the listener is removed.

experiments.name: refuse-iframe
experiments.purpose: Check whether a same-origin child frame with beforeunload protects the top guest.
experiments.expectation: The guest survives because the child frame refuses unload.

experiments.name: refuse-gesture
experiments.purpose: Check whether sticky user activation changes refusal under webContents.close.
experiments.expectation: With activation, the guest still survives the protected close.

experiments.name: cdp-deny-gesture
experiments.purpose: Test CDP Page.close({runBeforeUnload:true}) + Page.javascriptDialogOpening + Page.handleJavaScriptDialog(accept:false), with activation.
experiments.expectation: The beforeunload dialog opens, deny keeps the guest alive and scriptable, including after detaching the debugger.

experiments.name: cdp-accept-gesture
experiments.purpose: Control for CDP: accepting the beforeunload dialog must close the guest.
experiments.expectation: The dialog opens and accept:true destroys the guest.

experiments.name: cdp-deny-no-gesture
experiments.purpose: Check whether the CDP beforeunload dialog is available without user activation.
experiments.expectation: Without activation the dialog is skipped and the guest closes, so deny is impossible.

experiments.name: cdp-deny-inline
experiments.purpose: Remove the polling race by replying deny inside the CDP dialogOpening message handler itself.
experiments.expectation: Even an immediate deny keeps the guest alive and scriptable; if it is still destroyed, the CDP close path cannot be cancelled at all.

experiments.name: window-close-default
experiments.purpose: Control: does the same close option honour a refusal for a normal BrowserWindow WebContents (not a webview guest)?
experiments.expectation: The documented behaviour (page prevents unload => WebContents is not closed) holds for a BrowserWindow, isolating any failure to webview guests.

experiments.name: race-late-protection
experiments.purpose: Check the asynchronous protection-change race: the page installs a handler 150ms after the protected close starts.
experiments.expectation: The close is already in flight, so the guest is destroyed and the late handler never takes effect.

conclusion.cancellableSafePath: No tested native close path was both cancellable and usable for webview guests: webContents.close({waitForBeforeUnload:true}) destroys the guest despite will-prevent-unload, and CDP Page.close({runBeforeUnload:true}) destroys it even when the beforeunload dialog is explicitly denied. The same close option kept a BrowserWindow WebContents alive, so the failure is specific to webview guests. A production safe-close gate is unsupported for this runtime.
conclusion.recommendation: Keep the production safe-close gate unsupported for webview guests in this runtime: no tested close path can be cancelled or denied, so an attempted safe close destroys a refusing guest. Do not advertise P2b-style cancellable close for guests.
statements: webContents.close({waitForBeforeUnload:true}) kept a refusing guest alive (documented CloseOpts behaviour): false.
will-prevent-unload fired while the guest was still destroyed by the protected close: true.
Calling preventDefault on will-prevent-unload permitted the close: true.
Same-origin child-frame refusal protected the guest: false.
User activation changed refusal under webContents.close: false.
CDP beforeunload dialog opened with activation: true.
CDP deny kept the guest alive after detach: false.
Inline CDP deny (no polling) kept the guest alive: false.
CDP beforeunload dialog was denied yet the guest was still destroyed: true.
CDP accept closed the guest: true.
CDP dialog was skipped without activation: true.
Late protection lost the race: true.
The same close option kept a BrowserWindow WebContents alive: true.
supportScope: Hidden fixture BrowserWindow; sandboxed, context-isolated <webview> guests on a loopback HTTP origin.
Close initiated through webContents.close({waitForBeforeUnload:true}) or the guest debugger CDP Page.close({runBeforeUnload:true}).
Protection installed synchronously by the page before the close attempt (onbeforeunload or addEventListener), plus one late-protection race.
Same-origin top-level fixture pages only; no production LyShell UI, no user pages, no cross-origin frames, no service workers.
limitations: Three rounds per experiment; timing values are observations, not latency percentiles.
Hidden window and synthetic (CDP Input) activation; visible/focused-window behavior and real hardware input were not tested.
Only close-triggered beforeunload was tested, not navigation/reload-triggered unload.
Cross-origin child frames, sandboxed iframes without allow-same-origin, and OOPIF beforeunload paths were not tested.
CDP is an automation surface; attaching the debugger to a production guest is itself an operational cost and can be detached by DevTools or target destruction.
The probe records one Electron build (43.7.11) and must be rerun after any Electron upgrade.
